images.title: Read the scale first
images.purpose: Show that a bar 12 units long can stand for far more than 12 when one unit stands for 100.
images.composition: One long horizontal bar centred, with a label above its first unit and a line below.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal bar of exactly 12 equal units in a row with thin white gaps. The first unit is amber #E69F00, the other 11 are teal #0072B2. Above the first unit a label: 1 unit = 100 vehicles. Below the bar, centred, in reddish purple #CC79A7: 12 × 100 = 1200 vehicles. Exactly 1 bar, 12 units.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a bar with a number of units other than 12
images.takeaway: Read the scale first, then multiply the units by it.
images.description: A bar of 12 units with the first unit marked 1 unit = 100 vehicles, and the line 12 × 100 = 1200 vehicles.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say what one unit stands for before reading the length.

image_decisions.why: Reading a scale is a picture idea; one scaled bar carries it.
